changes.text: 8日，联邦一方的格兰特随己方的波托马克军跟在李的后面追击；李是南军北弗吉尼亚军团的统帅。格兰特正犯着重头痛，在路边一处离大部队有一段距离的农舍过夜，把脚泡进热水和芥末，手腕和后颈贴上芥末膏，指望天亮就能好。李来信提议会面，但按格兰特的说法，会面的目的并不是交出军队。格兰特的回信很干脆：他无权谈和，这样的会面不可能有好结果；和平的条件众所周知，南方只要放下武器，就能让和平早点到来，救下成千上万条人命和数以亿计尚未被毁的财产。

On the 8th Grant, on the Union side, followed his Army of the Potomac in pursuit, in rear of Lee, the commander of the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia. Grant was in the grip of a sick headache. He spent the night at a farmhouse on the road, some distance behind the main body of the army, bathing his feet in hot water and mustard and putting mustard plasters on his wrists and the back of his neck, hoping that by morning he would be cured. A letter from Lee proposed a meeting, but, as Grant tells it, for a different purpose from that of surrendering his army. Grant's answer was brisk. He had no authority to treat on the subject of peace, and the proposed meeting could lead to no good. The terms on which peace could be had, he wrote, were well understood: let the South lay down its arms, and the most desirable event would come sooner, sparing thousands of lives and hundreds of millions of property not yet destroyed.

后来李约见格兰特，按格兰特的记述，是为了拿到格兰特准备给他军队的条件。作者认为，难处在于具体的受降条文得由格兰特自己当场起草。基本条件已见于格兰特8日的信，李说自己就是这样理解的；但条文得由格兰特落笔写成。格兰特最后写下的那份条款里，有两处是落笔之后才想起来加进去的：军官的佩刀，以及军官的私马和私物。南军士兵自己的马骡则根本不在条文里：李问起时，格兰特先答以按条文不行，李表示明白，格兰特随后主动口头准许。

Later Lee asked Grant for an interview, as Grant records, for the purpose of getting from him the terms he proposed to give Lee's army. In the writer's view, the difficulty was that the actual terms of surrender were Grant's to draft on the spot. The basic conditions had already appeared in Grant's letter of the 8th, and Lee said he had so understood it; but the written clauses were Grant's to set down. Two items in the terms he finally set down were afterthoughts, added only once his pen was already moving: the officers' side-arms, and the officers' private horses and effects. The horses and mules belonging to the Confederate enlisted men were not in the written terms at all: when Lee asked, Grant first answered that as written they could not be kept; Lee said that was clear, and Grant then offered on his own, verbally, to let the men take them home.

格兰特回信拒绝会面之后，李再次来信，可这封信送得很费劲：由于格兰特所走的路线，这封信很可能无法在约定时间内送到他手里并带回答复，除非信使穿过南军战线。因此，李派人护送带信的军官穿过自己的战线，把信送到格兰特手里。另据格兰特记述，他这一方的两位指挥官米德和谢里登都对是否停火非常犹豫，怕这不是真心求和；而且李的北弗吉尼亚军团已无路可逃，除非用诡计脱身。不过他们最终同意停火两小时，以便在这段时间里设法与格兰特联络。

After Grant's refusal, Lee wrote again, but this message was hard to deliver: from the route Grant had taken, it would probably not be possible to reach him and get an answer back within the time fixed unless the messenger passed through the rebel lines. Lee therefore sent an escort with the officer bearing the message through his own lines to Grant. Separately, Grant records that Meade and Sheridan, two commanders on his own side, both hesitated very considerably about suspending hostilities at all. They were afraid the overture was not in good faith; and Lee's Army of Northern Virginia was where it could not escape except by some deception. They finally consented, however, to a suspension of hostilities for two hours, to give an opportunity of communicating with Grant in that time if possible.
格兰特收到信时还在头痛，一看到信的内容就好了。他回信说，因为自己改走了另一条路，上午11点50分才拿到信；他正向前赶去会面，请对方在他所走的这条路上通知会面地点。赶到谢里登那里时，那里的人情绪激动，表示认为这是南军脱身的诡计：他们相信，约翰斯顿正从北卡罗来纳北上，李则是要去与这位约翰斯顿会合；只要格兰特点头，五分钟内就能把对方打垮。格兰特不怀疑李的诚意，不久便被领到李所在之处。

The officer found Grant still suffering with the sick headache; in Grant's own telling, "the instant I saw the contents of the note I was cured." He wrote back at once. Lee's note had reached him only at 11:50 a.m., he explained, because he had switched to a different road; he would push forward to the front for the meeting, and a message left on the road he was on, naming the place, would reach him. When he rode up to Sheridan's position, the men there were very much excited. They expressed their view that the whole thing was a ruse to let the Confederates get away. They believed that Johnston was marching up from North Carolina, and that Lee was moving to join this Johnston; and they would whip the rebels where they stood in five minutes if only Grant would let them go in. Grant had no doubt of Lee's good faith, and was soon conducted to where he was.

此前两人没有一个字谈到私产、佩刀或类似问题。李看来对最初提出的条件并无异议；或者即便有意见，也想等条件写成文字再提。李读到佩刀、马匹和军官私物这一段时，说这会对他的军队有良好影响；格兰特说他讲这话时带着感情，并注明那只是自己当时的看法。至于流传甚广的李献剑、格兰特再把剑退回，格兰特把这件事以及关于它的许多其他说法直斥为“纯属虚构的传奇”：直到他把这一句写进条文，两人都没提过剑或佩刀，这不是预谋，是写到那里才想起来的。他还说，假如自己碰巧漏写、而李提了出来，他也会把这一项照样写进条款，就像他同意让士兵留下马匹那一条一样。

Not one word had passed between the two men about private property, side-arms or anything of the kind. Lee appeared to have no objection to the terms first proposed, or if he had a point against them he preferred to wait until they were in writing. When he read the passage about side-arms, horses and the officers' private property, he remarked with some feeling, Grant thought, that this would have a happy effect upon his army. As for the famous story of Lee surrendering his sword and Grant handing it back, Grant dismissed it, and much else that had been said about it, as "the purest romance." Until he wrote it into the terms, neither man had mentioned sword or side-arms. There was no premeditation: the thought did not occur to him until the moment he set it down. Had he happened to omit it and Lee called his attention to it, he said, he would have put it in precisely as he acceded to the provision about the soldiers keeping their horses.
马骡的宽许不在已写成的条文里，是格兰特当面对李承诺、将指示留守军官办理的。格兰特记下由吉本、格里芬、梅里特负责宣誓遣散，李留下朗斯特里特、戈登、彭德尔顿与之协商；但本文所据的段落没有写宣誓遣散和马骡宽许的实际执行经过。日期大多按原文「the 8th」这样的写法转述；原文所录电报注明的日期是1865年4月9日。

The indulgence on horses and mules was not in the terms as written; Grant promised Lee he would instruct the officers left behind to allow it. Grant records that Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated to carry out the paroling, with Lee leaving Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton for them to confer with; but the passages this piece draws on do not describe how the paroling or the horse-and-mule allowance was actually carried out. Dates are mostly kept as the source has them — "the 8th" and the like; the telegraph the source reproduces is dated April 9th, 1865.
全文只有一个史源，即格兰特本人的回忆记述。对话是他的转述，未必逐字；他明言不知李的心情；本文不替任何一方补写心理；马骡宽许不在已写成的条文中，是格兰特当面答应李将指示留守军官办理的，本文所据段落未交代其落实情况；原文记有宣誓遣散的执行人员安排，但本文所据段落未写执行经过；日期大多按原文写法转述，原文所录电报注明1865年4月9日。

There is only one source for this piece: Grant's own account in his memoirs. The conversations are his retellings and need not be verbatim; he says expressly that he did not know Lee's feelings, and this piece does not supply psychology for either side; the allowance on horses and mules was not in the written terms but promised to Lee as an instruction to the officers left behind, and its implementation is not reported in the passages used here; the source records who was assigned to carry out the paroling, but the passages used here do not say how it was carried out; dates are mostly kept in the original wording, and the telegraph the source reproduces is dated April 9th, 1865.

dispositions.rationale: 在格兰特、李首次出现时补充身份：格兰特属联邦一方、随己方波托马克军跟在李后面追击；李是南军北弗吉尼亚军团的统帅。波托马克军只出现一次，并说明属格兰特一方。中英同步，ev 补入 E28、E18。

General Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia
every man of the Confederate army

dispositions.rationale: 段首加过渡：后来李约见，是为了拿到格兰特给他军队的条件。把指代不清的 his/“他”改为 Grant's/“格兰特”，并删去与过渡句重复的“李要的是格兰特开出的条件”。其余事实与限定不变。

evidence.quote: he had asked for this interview for the purpose of getting from me the terms I proposed to give his army

dispositions.rationale: 段首对回信内容的重复压缩为“格兰特回信拒绝会面之后”。注明米德、谢里登是格兰特一方的两位指挥官，并把北弗吉尼亚军团写作“李的北弗吉尼亚军团”。中英同步。

evidence.quote: both of these commanders hesitated very considerably
General Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia

dispositions.rationale: 两条路名概括为“改走了另一条路”，删去沃克教堂以西约四英里的里程，保留11点50分收信。约翰斯顿只按证据说明为北军认为正从北卡罗来纳北上、李要去会合的人，没有加入证据外的身份。中英同步。

dispositions.rationale: 英文把斥为虚构的范围收窄为献剑一事及与之相关的说法：and much else that had been said about it。现与中文一致；中文原本准确，照原文重新给出。

evidence.quote: this and much more that has been said about it is the purest romance

两处对原文整体的断言收窄为“本文所据段落未交代/未写”/not reported in the passages used here、the passages used here do not say。
